A2A server combined user and workspace settings with a shallow spread, so a workspace fileFiltering: { respectGitIgnore: false } would erase the user's enableRecursiveFileSearch: true entirely.

prs.title: fix: prevent orphaned processes from consuming 100% CPU when terminal closes
prs.author: yuvrajangadsingh
prs.body:
Summary
This PR fixes issues #15874 and #15873 where closing the terminal window causes orphaned Gemini CLI processes to spin at 100% CPU, making the system unresponsive.
Root Cause
When a terminal is closed, the shell sends SIGHUP to child processes. Without proper signal handling, the CLI process continues running but loses its controlling terminal, causing it to spin in a tight loop trying to read from a closed TTY.
Solution
This PR implements a two-layer defense:

Signal Handlers (setupSignalHandlers): Handles SIGHUP, SIGTERM, and SIGINT signals with graceful shutdown
TTY Check (setupTtyCh

prs.title: feat: improve InputPrompt component functionality
prs.author: mohab-kamle
prs.body:
TLDR
Fixes a bug where the input box vanishes while the model is generating a response.
Now, the input box remains visible and active, allowing users to type concurrently.
This improves workflow by removing the strict stop-and-wait interaction.
Dive Deeper
Previously, the input component was being unmounted during response generation.

issues.title: Maintain alternating chat history for empty or thought-only model responses
issues.author: mrcabbage972
issues.body:
What happened?
The issue is a flaw in the recordHistory method's logic. When the model's response contained only non-visible content (like a thought part), the method would filter it out but then fail to add a placeholder empty model turn. This would either leave two consecutive user turns in the history (in streaming mode) or simply an incomplete turn, causing tests to fail and breaking conversational integrity.
What did you expect to happen?
The user and model turns should alternate.

workflows.
Steps to Reproduce

Initialize a git repository in the project directory (git init).
Instruct the Gemini CLI to modify or create a file.

Example User Prompt: "Create a new file named test.txt with the content
'hello world'"
